applicants.name: Julian Cox
applicants.activities: Built a calibration log for the robotics team and tutored two beginners through sensor tests. Worked 2 hours per week for 12 weeks; balanced the project with a weekend grocery shift.
applicants.essay: A wheel encoder counted turns while the robot stood still. I recorded ten trials before blaming the code. This happened after school. I learned that explaining a failed test can help a team more than presenting a perfect result. My next step was to write a checklist another student could test.
applicants.provenance: Authored synthetic scenario; profile and application decisions are not historical records.

applicants.name: Wyatt Campbell
applicants.activities: Ran a library programming workshop using paper algorithms before introducing Python. Worked 3 hours per week for 13 weeks; balanced the project with school orchestra rehearsals.
applicants.essay: A participant could follow my code but could not explain the loop. I replaced the screen with numbered cards. This happened at a Saturday workshop. Teaching made me notice the assumptions I had hidden inside my own explanations. My next step was to write a checklist another student could test.
applicants.provenance: Authored synthetic scenario; profile and application decisions are not historical records.

applicants.name: James Lee
applicants.activities: Redesigned the robotics club website for keyboard navigation and coached classmates in HTML. Worked 4 hours per week for 14 weeks; balanced the project with caring for a younger sibling.
applicants.essay: Our event form trapped keyboard users inside a menu. I asked a classmate to test without a mouse. This happened during our spring showcase. I began treating accessibility as a design requirement rather than a final checklist. My next step was to write a checklist another student could test.
applicants.provenance: Authored synthetic scenario; profile and application decisions are not historical records.

applicants.name: Jack Wilson
applicants.activities: Wrote a small inventory tool for a food pantry and taught volunteers how to check its totals. Worked 5 hours per week for 15 weeks; balanced the project with cross-country practice.
applicants.essay: Two volunteers entered the same delivery. I added a receipt identifier and a visible correction history. This happened with a new club member. A useful program must let people recognize and repair its mistakes. My next step was to write a checklist another student could test.
applicants.provenance: Authored synthetic scenario; profile and application decisions are not historical records.

applicants.name: Henry Collins
applicants.activities: Created a troubleshooting notebook for the robotics team and hosted lunchtime debugging sessions. Worked 6 hours per week for 16 weeks; balanced the project with debate club meetings.
applicants.essay: The senior programmer graduated with the only working setup on a laptop. I rebuilt the instructions on a clean machine. This happened before a community open house. applicants.provenance: Authored synthetic scenario; profile and application decisions are not historical records.

applicants.name: Luke Cook
applicants.activities: Logged readings from a school water sensor and taught younger robotics members to plot measurements. Worked 2 hours per week for 17 weeks; balanced the project with a school newspaper role.
